subject.title: Auto-update can leave running gateway with stale hashed bundle imports

question: For stale OpenClaw-owned hashed imports after an update, should the supported contract be prevention at the controlled update layer only, or also a bounded one-shot runtime restart for processes disrupted by out-of-band file rotation?
rationale: The available evidence establishes distinct controlled and uncontrolled update paths with materially different failure and recovery semantics; choosing whether runtime recovery is a supported availability guarantee is a product and operational-policy decision.

options.title: Strengthen controlled updates and report unsupported swaps
options.body: Retain prior generations through managed handoff, then emit a clear restart-required state when an out-of-band replacement invalidates a loaded module graph.

options.title: Add bounded stale-chunk self-restart
options.body: Recognize only missing OpenClaw-owned hashed siblings and trigger one controlled restart with loop protection and visible diagnostics.

options.title: Externalize package replacement
options.body: Sponsor the external-updater direction in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77511 and use it as the long-term owner of package rotation.

recommendation.title: Strengthen controlled updates and report unsupported swaps
recommendation.body: Retain prior generations through managed handoff, then emit a clear restart-required state when an out-of-band replacement invalidates a loaded module graph.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is assigned to the issue and is the best available routing point for the explicit update-lifecycle decision.
